study_units.title: Imaging Modality Principles (X-Ray/Fluoroscopy, Computed Tomography, Ultrasound, MRI, PET-CT): Physics, Indications, and Relative Radiation Exposure
study_units.structural_rationale: MI.S01's printed title 'ACTOMYMS' (OCR-garbled 'ACRONYMS') merges a non-clinical acronym glossary (confirmed at pdf 792/MI2: FDG, eGFR, LUQ, ADC, etc.) with the genuine 'Imaging Modalities' heading (merged_duplicate_headings). Body confirmation (clean-ocr 0792-0793) shows five foundational modality-physics topics: X-Ray Imaging (plain film, fluoroscopy), Computed Tomography (Hounsfield units, windowing), Ultrasound (echogenicity, Doppler), and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (T1/T2 relaxation), plus a typical-effective-dose comparison table. Positron Emission Tomography Scans content is body-confirmed at pdf 793/MI3. Consolidated into one SUPPORTING_KNOWLEDGE unit since these are foundational modality-physics/classification topics underlying every subsequent organ-system unit in the chapter, analogous to chapter ID's 'Principles of Microbiology' precedent (SU-ID-01). The acronym glossary itself is non-clinical and not separately represented.

study_units.title: Contrast Agents and Contrast Safety (Iodinated Contrast, Gadolinium, Barium, Microbubbles; Contrast-Induced Nephropathy Prevention)
study_units.structural_rationale: MI.S01's fifth T-child 'Contrast Agents', body-confirmed at the top of pdf 794/MI4 (Table 2: barium, iodinated agents, gadolinium chelates, microbubbles - advantages/disadvantages/contraindications for each), including the adjacent margin notes on methods to reduce contrast-induced nephropathy risk and contraindications to IV contrast (myasthenia gravis, prior adverse reaction, renal impairment, dehydration, heart failure) confirmed at pdf 793/MI3. Represented as its own DIRECT unit, distinct from SU-MI-01's foundational physics content, because contrast safety (contraindications, nephropathy prevention) is independently and concretely testable per project scope priorities, unlike the general modality-physics background.

study_units.title: Chest X-Ray Views and Chest CT Approach (Technique, Systematic Interpretation, Windowing)
study_units.structural_rationale: MI.S02's printed title 'Chestlmaging' is a wrapped-heading defect (missing space) for 'Chest Imaging', confirmed genuine and coherent at pdf 794/MI4. First two T-children body-confirmed: Chest X-Ray (standard views PA/lateral/AP/lateral decubitus/lordotic, pdf 794/MI4; systematic ABCDEF approach and anatomy legend, pdf 795-796/MI5-6) and Chest Computed Tomography (soft tissue/bone/lung windowing approach, standard/low-dose/CTA scan types, pdf 796/MI6).

study_units.title: Recognition of Airspace and Parenchymal Lung Abnormalities (Atelectasis, Consolidation/Pneumonia, Pulmonary Nodule)
study_units.structural_rationale: Part of MI.S02.T03 'Lung Abnormalities', body-confirmed at pdf 797/MI7 (Atelectasis pathogenesis/findings/differential, Consolidation) through pdf 798/MI8 (Pulmonary Nodule benign vs. malignant characteristics, Fleischner-guideline follow-up). Split from SU-MI-05 (Interstitial Disease, same T-child) because the two represent distinct, independently body-confirmed subheadings within this single TOC node, per the project convention of splitting broad nodes only when body evidence supports it (cf. chapter GY's Fibroids/Contraception precedent); atelectasis/consolidation/nodule recognition is core generalist-relevant content, whereas interstitial disease's extensive differential is comparatively specialist (see SU-MI-05).

study_units.title: Interstitial Lung Disease Imaging Patterns
study_units.structural_rationale: Continuation of MI.S02.T03 'Lung Abnormalities', body-confirmed at pdf 797/MI7: 'Interstitial Disease' with septal-thickening (Kerley lines), nodular, and reticular imaging patterns, and an extensive occupational/autoimmune/drug-related/infectious/idiopathic differential (FASSTEN, BAD RASH mnemonics). Represented separately from SU-MI-04 per the same node-splitting convention; classified SPECIALIST_DETAIL given the differential's granularity exceeds core MCCQE scope, though the underlying dyspnea/cough presentation is still covered generally by SU-MI-04's evidence.
